item.text:
**Supported facts**

To make `Bun.WebView` connect to an already-running Chrome-family browser over CDP WebSocket, Bun’s docs show the `backend` object form with a Chrome `url`, for example:

```ts
new Bun.WebView({
  backend: {
    type: "chrome",
    url: "ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/abc123...",
  },
});
```

This is documented in Bun’s WebView guide under “Connecting to an already-running Chrome.”  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The same page says the Chrome `backend.url` option is a Chrome-only `ws://` URL for an existing Chrome DevTools endpoint, and that `url: false` disables auto-detect and forces Bun to spawn its own browser instead.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The docs also say Bun may auto-detect an already-running Chrome-family browser by reading `DevToolsActivePort` from standard profile directories; if found, Bun connects over WebSocket instead of spawning a new browser.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The docs say an explicit `url: "ws://..."` does **not** fall back to spawning if the connection fails; in that case, the connection failure throws.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The docs say `url: "ws://..."` cannot be combined with `path` or `argv`, and that passing `path` or `argv` implies spawn mode and skips auto-detect.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

For enabling remote debugging on a running Chrome, Bun’s docs say you can use `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` or launch Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

**Documented lifecycle operations**

The official Lifecycle section documents `view.close()` as a lifecycle operation. Bun says it is synchronous and idempotent, destroys the page’s renderer process, rejects pending promises with `Error("WebView closed")`, and causes later method calls to throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The docs also say `view[Symbol.dispose]` and `view[Symbol.asyncDispose]` both point to `close()`, so `using` and `await using` perform automatic cleanup.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The official Lifecycle section also documents `Bun.WebView.closeAll()` as a lifecycle operation. Bun says it force-kills the Chrome subprocess and the WebKit host subprocess, rejects pending promises on the next event-loop tick, and allows later `new Bun.WebView()` calls to respawn browsers as needed.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The API reference repeats these callable lifecycle methods as `close()` on instances and `WebView.closeAll()` on the class.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

**Inference**

It is reasonable to treat the explicit lifecycle **operations** as only `close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`, because those are the callable actions documented in the Lifecycle section; “Event-loop behavior” and “Subprocess death” are documented lifecycle behaviors, not callable operations. This classification is my interpretation of the docs’ structure, not a sentence Bun states verbatim.  
Source for underlying section structure: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

The example URL `ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/...` strongly indicates a browser-level CDP endpoint rather than a tab/session endpoint, and that fits the docs’ statement that Bun connects once to Chrome and then creates tabs with `Target.createTarget`. That browser-level wording is therefore supported by the example and surrounding behavior, but the exact phrase “browser-level CDP WebSocket URL” is my synthesis.  
Source: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview

**Disagreement**

No conflicting statement was found in the official Bun WebView docs I reviewed.

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

I did not find a separate official Bun page that adds more lifecycle operations beyond `close()` and `Bun.WebView.closeAll()`. The API reference page for `Bun.WebView` is consistent with the runtime WebView page but does not appear to expand the lifecycle list.  
Sources: https://bun.sh/docs/runtime/webview , https://bun.sh/reference/bun/WebView
